title: Extract Frames from Video – Save Stills as PNG or JPG
description: Save the paused frame of a video, a picture every few seconds, or frames spread evenly, as PNG or JPG files. Done in your browser, no upload.
heading: Extract Frames from a Video
subtitle: Save the frame you paused on, or many frames as one ZIP of PNG or JPG pictures, without uploading the video.
intro: Grab a sharp still for a thumbnail, a slide or a report straight from the video, at the video's own resolution. Pause the player on the moment you want and save that frame, or take a picture every few seconds, or a set number of pictures spread evenly over the whole video for a contact sheet. The page says how many pictures it will make before you start; several come as one ZIP file.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your browser takes the pictures from the video on your device; nothing is uploaded.

features.title: Full resolution
features.text: Frames are saved at the video's own size, or at a width you choose, as lossless PNG or smaller JPG.

features.title: One frame or hundreds
features.text: The paused frame, one every few seconds, or a number spread evenly; up to 500 pictures in one ZIP.

stepsTitle: How to extract frames from a video

steps.title: Add your video
steps.text: Choose or drop an MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV file; it opens in the player.

steps.title: Choose the frames
steps.text: Pick This frame and pause on the moment, or Every few seconds, or a number spread evenly.

steps.title: Pick format and size
steps.text: Choose PNG or JPG and, if you like, a largest width.

steps.title: Save and download
steps.text: Click Save and download one picture, or one ZIP with all of them.

handlesTitle: Videos and picture formats it handles
handles: Videos: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV and other files your browser can play.
Pictures: PNG (lossless) or JPG, at the video's size or at most 1920, 1280, 640 or 320 pixels wide.
Choices: the paused frame, one picture every 1 to 60 seconds, or 1 to 500 pictures spread evenly.
Names: each picture in the ZIP is named with its number and its time in the video, like clip-0003-2_00s.png.
limits: At most 500 pictures at a time; choose a longer gap or fewer pictures for long videos.
A picture is the frame shown at that moment, so a fast-moving scene can look blurred, as it does when paused.
Videos in a format your browser can't play can't be read; the page says so and suggests Chrome or Edge.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the video and makes the pictures on your device; nothing is sent anywhere. Your browser's network panel shows no upload.

faq.question: How do I save one exact frame?
faq.answer: Choose This frame, play the video and pause it on the moment you want (you can drag the player's bar), then click Save the picture.

faq.question: Should I choose PNG or JPG?
faq.answer: PNG keeps every pixel and suits screenshots, text and editing. JPG files are much smaller and suit photos and sharing.

faq.question: Why at most 500 pictures?
faq.answer: Every picture is kept in memory until the ZIP is made, and full-size frames are large. For long videos, choose a gap of a few seconds.

faq.question: What resolution are the frames?
faq.answer: The video's own size, such as 1920 × 1080 for a Full HD video, unless you choose a largest width. A small video is never enlarged.
